newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil settles down $5.75, Brent 15 cts highe.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil settles down $5.75, Brent 15 cts highe.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed down $5.75 on Thursday on technically-inspired selling that took the market out of line with firmer Brent and U.S. heating oil, traders said.
Front month April futures settled at $166.75 after hitting a high in the morning of $169.75.
"Gas oil was under pressure and had a breakdown technically," a broker said.
Support was breached at $168 a barrel in the morning "and then we were in open territory with the next support really at $165.25", a trader said. April hit a low of $166.50.
Brokers GNI in a daily report noted that the fact that several refineries announced the end of turnaround on Wednesday was negative for products.

Charles Gray of Prudential Bache International said that while Monday was the last trading day for NYMEX gasoline and heating oil, Friday was in effect the day when most speculative positions would be squared.
April heating oil was 0.37 cent stronger at 55.80 cents a gallon. Gasoline was 0.47 cent adrift at 64.35 cents a gallon.

May IPE Brent was 16 cents firmer at a new high of $19.45 a barrel at 1751 GMT, having recovered from weakness seen around the NYMEX opening, largely on concern over disruption to Shell production in Nigeria.
Uncertainty about Nigerian political unrest also helped the IPE contract to resist earlier NYMEX-inspired downward pressure.
"People will not want to go short over the long weekend while the Nigerian problems continue," a trader said.
Brokers continued to peg resistance on May IPE at around $19.50 and $19.61, with support at around the day's low of $19.20 and then at $18.83.
Shell said on Thursday a seventh oil installation on the Niger Delta was occupied last Saturday by villagers, forcing the oil giant to cut back production by a total of 210,000 barrels per day (bpd).
A senior official at Nigeria National Petroleum Corp said that Shell could declare force majeure on early April cargoes.
